summary:
The Burmese Narrow-headed Softshell Turtle once moved silently through the great rivers of Myanmar — the Ayeyarwady, the Chindwin, the Salween — a flat, ghostly presence in the current, shaped by millions of years of evolution. Rarely seen and little understood, it belongs to an ancient lineage that outlasted the dinosaurs, only to face its gravest threat in a single human lifetime.

Since the mid-1990s, relentless harvesting for the international food trade has driven populations down by an estimated 80% or more. Gold mining, poisoned waters, and fishing conflicts have compounded the loss. Critically Endangered and still declining, this elusive turtle now exists at the edge — a quiet disappearance from rivers that have flowed long before us, and may outlast us still.
